# DocsGPT

> DocsGPT is an open-source platform for building AI agents and assistants with document retrieval, tools, and
> multi-model support. Run it with Docker, pip or Kubernetes, with hosted or local models.

This file maps the DocsGPT documentation for LLMs and coding agents. It is generated from the docs sidebar by
`docs/scripts/generate-llms.mjs`; don't edit it by hand.

## Overview

- [Home](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/): Documentation for DocsGPT, the open-source platform for building AI agents and assistants with document retrieval, tools and multi-model support.
- [Quickstart](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/quickstart): Install and start DocsGPT with one command, or from a clone with the setup script.
- [Upgrading](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/upgrading): Upgrade DocsGPT installed with the installer, pip, Docker Compose or Kubernetes, and what changes in each release.
- [Changelog](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/changelog): What changed in each DocsGPT release, with links to the upgrade steps an existing deployment needs.

## Concepts

- [Concepts](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Concepts): The words the DocsGPT docs and web app use - agents, knowledge and sources, chunks, connectors and connections, tools, workflows, prompts, teams, and the credentials that call the API.
- [Architecture](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Concepts/Architecture): How DocsGPT connects clients, agents, retrieval, background workers, models, and storage.

## Using DocsGPT

- [Using the Web App](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Using/web-app): Find your way around the DocsGPT web app - the sidebar, conversation search with Ctrl/Cmd+K, the agent library with folders, pinning and templates, importing an agent from YAML, and the General settings for theme, language and the active prompt.
- [Sharing Conversations](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Using/sharing): Share a conversation as a public, read-only page or as a page where anyone with the link can keep asking questions on your account, and how to stop a link.
- [Teams and Sharing](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Using/teams-and-sharing): Create a team, add members, give them roles, and share agents, sources, prompts and tools with a team or one teammate as a viewer or an editor.
- [Analytics and Logs](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Using/analytics-and-logs): Read the Analytics charts, filter the Logs list and open an execution trace in the DocsGPT web app, for your whole account or for one agent.

## Agents

- [Agent Basics](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Agents/basics): Learn about DocsGPT Agents, their types, how to create and manage them, and how they can enhance your interaction with documents and tools.
- [Workflow Nodes](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Agents/nodes): The nodes a DocsGPT workflow is built from - Start, AI Agent, End, Note, Set State, If / Else and Code - and the shared state they read and write.
- [Schedules](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Agents/schedules): Run an agent on a timer - recurring schedules and one-time tasks from the Schedules tab, tasks set from chat with the Scheduling tool, the run log, auto-pause, the REST API, the operator limits, and the beat scheduler every schedule needs.
- [Guardrails](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Agents/guardrails): Scan user input, retrieved sources, tool results and answers with built-in checks — PII, secrets, banned terms, link policy, prompt injection, groundedness and an LLM judge — and choose to flag, redact or block. Includes the audit journal, instance floor and API reference.
- [Customizing Prompts](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Agents/prompts): Write the prompts your chats and agents use - adding and editing them in Settings, the Jinja2 template variables (system, source, passthrough, tools, artifacts, attachments), how a prompt is assembled, and the built-in presets.
- [Context Compression](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Agents/context-compression): How DocsGPT summarizes long conversations to stay within the model's context window, and the settings that control it.
- [Benchmarking Agents](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Agents/benchmarking): Run repeatable benchmarks and evals against your DocsGPT agents from the terminal with docsgpt-cli bench.

## Knowledge

- [Add Knowledge](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Sources/adding-knowledge): Add files, web pages, GitHub repositories, wikis and synced services to Knowledge, then use them in chats and agents.
- [Document Parsing and OCR](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Sources/ocr): Which engine parses uploaded documents, how OCR works in DocsGPT, how to configure it, and what changes for source ingestion vs chat attachments.
- [Per-Source Configuration](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Sources/Per-source-configuration): Tune how each knowledge source is chunked at ingest time and retrieved at query time — chunking strategy, retriever, exposure, top-k, pre-screening and more.
- [GraphRAG](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Sources/GraphRAG): Build a knowledge graph from a source at ingest time and retrieve over it with Personalized PageRank. Covers requirements, enabling, configuration, and the graph view.
- [Wiki Sources](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Sources/Wiki-sources): Create a knowledge source that the agent can read and write — a living wiki it keeps up to date, with human edits, provenance stamps, and version safety.
- [Connectors Overview](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Sources/Connectors): Connect DocsGPT to the services your team uses. One connection can sync content into Knowledge and give agents tools, with credentials encrypted on the server.
- [Google Drive](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Sources/Connectors/google-drive): Connect your Google Drive as an external knowledge base to upload and process files directly from your Google Drive account.
- [SharePoint / OneDrive](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Sources/Connectors/sharepoint): Connect your Microsoft SharePoint or OneDrive as an external knowledge base to upload and process files directly.
- [Confluence](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Sources/Connectors/confluence): Connect your Confluence Cloud workspace as an external knowledge base to upload and process pages directly.
- [GitHub](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Sources/Connectors/github): Sync GitHub repositories into Knowledge and give agents GitHub's read-only MCP tools, with a personal access token or a GitHub App sign-in.
- [Linear](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Sources/Connectors/linear): Sign in to Linear once to give agents Linear's tools and sync issues and project documents into Knowledge.
- [Amazon S3](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Sources/Connectors/s3): Sync documents from an Amazon S3 bucket, or S3-compatible storage such as MinIO or Cloudflare R2, into Knowledge.

## Tools

- [Tools Basics](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Tools/basics): Understand what DocsGPT Tools are, how they work, and explore the built-in tools available to extend DocsGPT's functionality.
- [API Tool](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Tools/api-tool): Learn how to configure and use the API Tool in DocsGPT to connect with any RESTful API without writing custom code.
- [MCP Tools](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Tools/mcp-tools): Connect external tools to DocsGPT agents using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) standard.
- [Artifacts and Code Execution](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Tools/artifacts-and-code-execution): Generate editable documents, run sandboxed code, and read files with the DocsGPT artifact, code executor, and read document tools.
- [Remote Device](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Tools/remote-device): Run shell commands on a paired remote machine from a DocsGPT agent using docsgpt-cli host.
- [Creating a Custom Tool](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Tools/creating-a-tool): Learn how to create custom Python tools to extend DocsGPT's functionality and integrate with various services or perform specific actions.

## Models

- [Cloud Providers](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Models/cloud-providers): Connect DocsGPT to various Cloud Large Language Model (LLM) providers to power your document Q&A.
- [Local Inference](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Models/local-inference): Connect DocsGPT to local inference engines for running LLMs directly on your hardware.
- [Embeddings](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Models/embeddings): Learn about embedding models, their importance in DocsGPT, and how to configure them for optimal performance.
- [Custom Models](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Models/custom-models): Add your own OpenAI-compatible model in Settings → Custom Models - the fields, Test connection, where the model appears, how its API key is stored, why only public endpoints are allowed, and the /api/user/models endpoints.
- [Fallback Models](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Models/fallback): Switch to another model automatically when the primary model fails, and keep each provider's API key with that provider.

## API

- [API Overview](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/API): How to call the DocsGPT API — agent API keys, personal access tokens and session tokens, which page covers which endpoints, and where your instance serves its Swagger UI and OpenAPI document.
- [Agent API Keys](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/API/agent-keys): Learn how to obtain, understand, and use DocsGPT API keys to integrate DocsGPT into your external applications and widgets.
- [Personal Access Tokens](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/API/personal-access-tokens): Scoped, revocable API tokens for managing agents, sources and other DocsGPT resources from the CLI, scripts and CI/CD pipelines.
- [Agent API](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/API/agent-api): Learn how to programmatically interact with DocsGPT Agents using the streaming and non-streaming API endpoints.
- [OpenAI-Compatible API](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/API/openai-compatible): Connect any OpenAI-compatible client to DocsGPT Agents via /v1/chat/completions — streaming, structured output, files and images, tool calling, reasoning, and idempotent retries.
- [Agent Webhooks](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/API/webhooks): Learn how to automate and integrate DocsGPT Agents using webhooks for asynchronous task execution.
- [Realtime Events](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/API/realtime-events): Subscribe to DocsGPT's server-sent events channel for live notifications — ingestion progress, tool approvals, MCP OAuth completion — and reconnect to an in-flight chat answer.
- [MCP Server](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/API/mcp-server): Connect Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor or any MCP client to DocsGPT's own MCP server at /mcp and search an agent's sources with the search_docs tool, authenticated with the agent's API key.
- [REST API Reference](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/API/reference): Every endpoint in DocsGPT's Swagger document, with its parameters, request body fields and the personal access token scope it needs.

## Widgets & Integrations

- [Chat Widget](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Extensions/chat-widget): Embed the DocsGPT Widget in your React, HTML, or Nextra projects to provide AI-powered chat functionality to your users.
- [Search Widget](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Extensions/search-widget): Embed the DocsGPT Search Bar Widget in your React or HTML projects to provide AI-powered document search functionality to your users.
- [Chatwoot Extension](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Extensions/Chatwoot-extension): Answer incoming Chatwoot messages with a DocsGPT agent. Set up the agent key, the Chatwoot access token and webhook, then configure and run the bridge in extensions/chatwoot.
- [Community Integrations](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Extensions/community): Discord, Slack and Telegram bots and the docsgpt-cli terminal client - integrations that live in their own arc53 repositories and connect to DocsGPT with an agent API key.

## Deploy & Operate

- [Choose a Deployment](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Deploying): Compare the ways to install DocsGPT (installer, Docker Compose, pip, Kubernetes, air-gapped) and pick the one that fits.
- [Docker Setup](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Deploying/Docker-Deploying): Deploy DocsGPT using Docker and Docker Compose for easy setup and management.
- [Install with pip](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Deploying/Pip-Install): Run the DocsGPT backend from the PyPI package, inside your own Python environment.
- [Deploying on Kubernetes](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Deploying/Kubernetes-Deploying): Run DocsGPT on a Kubernetes cluster with the manifests in deployment/k8s - secrets, S3 and pgvector storage, migrations, publishing through an Ingress, and upgrades.
- [Air-Gapped Deployment](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Deploying/Air-Gapped): Run DocsGPT on a network with no internet access.
- [Code Execution Sandbox](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Deploying/Sandbox): Run the sandbox that the Artifact and Code Executor tools need - the self-hosted Jupyter runner with Docker Compose, Kubernetes or pip, or Daytona Cloud - with the gateway token, kernel settings and network isolation.
- [docsgpt CLI Reference](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Deploying/cli): Every docsgpt subcommand and its main options, for the installer, pip installs, the Docker image and a source checkout.
- [App Configuration](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Deploying/DocsGPT-Settings): Configure your DocsGPT application by understanding the basic settings.
- [Settings Reference](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Deploying/Settings-Reference): Every DocsGPT setting, grouped by domain, with its type, default and purpose.
- [Security Checklist](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Deploying/Security): Harden a DocsGPT install before other people or the internet can reach it - bind addresses, the choice of AUTH_TYPE, the secrets to set, outbound URL checks, prompt templates, the LLM cache and the version check.
- [SSO with OIDC](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Deploying/OIDC-SSO): Sign users into DocsGPT through any OpenID Connect identity provider (Authentik, Keycloak, Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, ...) — with group allowlists, silent session renewal, back-channel logout, and SCIM provisioning.
- [Access Control & Teams](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Deploying/Access-Control): How DocsGPT models permissions — global admin/user roles (RBAC), the admin dashboard, teams with per-team roles, and sharing agents, sources, prompts, and tools.
- [Usage Quotas](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Deploying/Usage-Quotas): Cap how many tokens or dollars each user may spend per day, week or month, with an instance default, per-team allowances and per-user overrides.
- [Observability](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Deploying/Observability): Send traces, metrics, and logs from DocsGPT to any OpenTelemetry-compatible backend (Axiom, Honeycomb, Grafana, Datadog, Jaeger, etc.).
- [Background Jobs & Retention](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Deploying/Background-Jobs): The periodic tasks the Celery beat scheduler runs in DocsGPT - source syncs, scheduled agent runs, reconciliation and cleanups - what each one trims and when, what is kept until someone deletes it, and how to make sure beat is running.
- [PostgreSQL for User Data](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Deploying/Postgres-Migration): PostgreSQL is the user-data store for DocsGPT. Covers auto-bootstrap, production hardening, and the one-shot migration from legacy MongoDB deployments.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Deploying/Troubleshooting): First checks for a DocsGPT install that misbehaves - docsgpt doctor, the logs to read, and the common symptoms with their causes, from searches that ignore your documents to notifications that never arrive.
- [SSE Notifications Runbook](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Deploying/Troubleshooting/sse-notifications): Diagnose missing notifications, a bell badge that never lights up, upload toasts that hang and chat answers that don't reconnect - Redis checks, the symptom map, failure modes and the realtime event settings.
- [Development Environment](https://docs.docsgpt.cloud/Deploying/Development-Environment): Guide to setting up a development environment for DocsGPT, including backend and frontend setup.
